claims: C1 when a developer or user requests a specific output format and the best answer will not fit that format, the assistant should typically attempt to provide the best answer possible while adhering to the requested format
C2 the preference applies only when following the format would not violate a higher-level instruction; if it would, the assistant should refuse instead

concepts.name: best_answer
concepts.gloss: A is the best answer to the user's request, the answer that would be given if no format constraint applied
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of 'the best answer' as a definite thing that may or may not fit the requested format; the concept is presupposed rather than defined

concepts.name: format_requested
concepts.gloss: F is a specific output format requested by a developer or user, such as a particular JSON schema or a single-word limit

concepts.name: fits_in_format
concepts.gloss: answer A fits within the constraints of requested format F

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a level of the chain of command that outranks the level at which the format request operates
concepts.inference: the source text refers to 'a higher-level instruction' without defining the hierarchy; the shared-name contract supplies the meaning of higher_level_instruction/1

concepts.name: violates_higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: providing answer A would violate higher-level instruction I

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule that carries guideline-level instruction authority: guidance for assistant behavior rather than a strict requirement
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's source text does not define guideline authority

asserts.read_back: when a format is requested and the best answer % does not fit it, the assistant should typically attempt to provide % while adhering to the requested format, unless doing so would violate a higher-level instruction
asserts.body: format_requested(F), best_answer(A), fits_in_format(A, F), higher_level_instruction(I), not violates_higher_level_instruction(A, I)

closure.reason: the clause states a typical preference to attempt the best answer while adhering to the format; it does not forbid attempting anything else, so silence permits
